Union Pacific releases video of CEO’s rate remarks at shipper conference
sum: OMAHA, Neb. — Union Pacific today released its video of CEO Jim Vena’s March shipper association speech, which includes his controversial remarks about raising rates for customers who opposed the UP-Norfolk Southern merger.

Vena touted the benefits of the merger during the 52-minute, 42-second video. At the end of the recording of the keynote address at the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers meeting, Vena said: “So bottom line is we’re going to get this done. It’s good for the country, good for our employees, and it’s good for all of you if you actually sit back and take a look at what we’re going to be able to offer. We’re willing to make deals with customers. So come and see us. Talk about what you need to move ahead with us and how we put this thing forward. If we don’t do that, Union Pacific will still be there. And if I stick around, which I probably will, I’ll probably increase everybody’s rates that said they didn’t want a seamless railroad by three or four extra percent to teach you a lesson. Thank you very much.”
The CEO then waved and walked offscreen at the end of the question-and-answer session.

The remarks prompted Sen. Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.) to write to the Surface Transportation Board in July to express concerns that UP was threatening to retaliate against shippers who didn’t back the merger. CPKC and a coalition of shipper groups subsequently sought to have the UP video made public as part of the merger review. And last week CPKC urged the STB to toss out the UP-NS merger application, arguing that Vena’s comments have made it impossible for regulators to develop a full evidentiary record because shippers are afraid to speak out.

The STB on Wednesday rejected UP’s appeal of an administrative law judge’s order to make the video public, ruling that the appeal was late and lacked merit. The board ordered UP to remove the video’s confidential designation and provide it to all parties by 5 p.m. Eastern today.
In a statement accompanying the video, UP sought to put the remarks into the context of the entire speech and encouraged shippers to participate in the merger review process.

items.t: Canadian singer-songwriter Tyler Shaw looking to secure spot in ‘world’s biggest live music event’
sum: A Canadian artist set to perform in Simcoe County is vying for a spot in an international music contest. Singer-songwriter Tyler Shaw, known for hits like “House of Cards,” “To the Man Who Let Her Go” and “With You,” is one of five Canadian artists who are contenders to represent Canada at the Eurovision Song Contest 2027. Hosted by the European Broadcasting Union,Eurovision is touted as “the world’s biggest live music event” where artists from around the world compete in the singing competition. The winner will receive a glass microphone trophy and their country will get the honour of hosting the event the following year. “It’s the Olympics of songwriting essentially,” Shaw tells CTV News in an exclusive interview. The competition not only puts a spotlight on the Canadian arts scene, but Shaw says this is a huge opportunity for him as it could give him the global recognition he’s looking for. “It opens up a lot of doors for artists here in Canada especially with this contest,” Shaw says. Members of the public can vote with Thursday being the last day. CPKC Holiday Train Not only is Shaw gearing up for Eurovision, but he’s also set to perform in our region on the CPKC Holiday Train. It’s making a whopping 50 stops. Once the train rolls in, an entire side of one of the cars folds down and transforms into a makeshift stage. He’s set to perform for around 15 minutes. Whether there are a handful of people or thousands gathered, Shaw says the energy is high. “When that happens, you just can’t stop the excitement, no matter how big or small the crowd is,” Shaw says. Shaw released his first album in 2015 and since then, he says if you pay attention to life, you can find inspiration everywhere. “The inspiration, it really does just follow my life,” Shaw says. But the last few years have especially given him something to write about. “Obviously becoming a father has opened up perspective over the last six years and just story-telling wise,” Shaw says. Shaw’s forthcoming album there’s no easy way to put this... will be out Feb. 19. The title track was released at the end of last month. The train will roll up in Springwater, MacTier and Parry Sound on Nov. 30.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City stock posts 15% Q3 revenue growth
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported third-quarter revenue of 4.219 billion Canadian dollars on October 28, up 15 percent from the same period a year earlier. The release from CPKC investor relations showed a mixed quarter: volumes improved, but fuel inflation pushed operating ratios higher.

Revenue ton-miles rose 6 percent in the three months ended September 30. Freight revenue reached 4.139 billion Canadian dollars, with grain revenue increasing to 904 million Canadian dollars from 702 million a year earlier and intermodal revenue rising to 815 million Canadian dollars from 668 million.

Reported operating expenses climbed to 2.732 billion Canadian dollars from 2.325 billion. Fuel expense was 667 million Canadian dollars, compared with 415 million in the prior-year quarter. The reported operating ratio increased to 64.8 percent from 63.5 percent, while the core adjusted ratio rose to 61.9 percent from 60.7 percent.

CPKC said higher fuel prices affected the reported and core adjusted operating ratios by 170 and 190 basis points, respectively. The company also reported diluted earnings per share of 1.04 Canadian dollars, compared with 1.01 Canadian dollars a year earlier. Core adjusted diluted earnings per share rose to 1.28 Canadian dollars from 1.10 Canadian dollars.

Net income was 916 million Canadian dollars, nearly unchanged from 917 million in the third quarter of 2025. The reported result included acquisition-related and other discrete tax items, including a 94 million Canadian dollar reassessment related to the Kansas City Southern acquisition. CPKC's adjusted figures exclude specified items and are not standardized under generally accepted accounting principles.

Chief Executive Officer Keith Creel said the railroad was running well and that service remained strong across grain, intermodal and merchandise markets. He said disciplined execution and the company's North American network kept CPKC on track to meet its commitments for 2026.

The company retained its full-year targets for low-double-digit growth in core adjusted diluted earnings per share and mid-single-digit growth in revenue ton-miles. Capital spending is planned at approximately 2.65 billion Canadian dollars.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City stock faces fuel test after Q3 growth
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported strong third-quarter growth on October 28, but higher fuel costs kept pressure on operating efficiency. In its earnings release, the railroad said revenue reached CAD 4.219 billion in the three months ended September 30, up 15 percent from CAD 3.661 billion a year earlier.

Volume, measured in revenue ton-miles, increased 6 percent. Reported diluted earnings per share rose 3 percent to CAD 1.04 from CAD 1.01, while core adjusted diluted earnings per share climbed 16 percent to CAD 1.28 from CAD 1.10. The adjusted figure is a non-GAAP measure and is therefore not directly comparable with every company reporting under standard accounting definitions.

The main pressure point was the operating ratio, where a lower percentage indicates better efficiency. CPKC's reported ratio increased to 64.8 percent from 63.5 percent, while the core adjusted ratio rose to 61.9 percent from 60.7 percent. The company said higher fuel prices affected the reported ratio by 170 basis points and the core adjusted ratio by 190 basis points.

Operating income nevertheless increased 11 percent to CAD 1.487 billion from CAD 1.336 billion. The company also reported freight revenue of CAD 4.139 billion, compared with CAD 3.589 billion in the third quarter of 2025. Grain and intermodal were among the growth areas highlighted by management, supporting the case that network expansion and pricing are offsetting part of the cost pressure.
Canadian Pacific Kansas City stock traded at 81.11 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 13:10 CET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Canadian Pacific Kansas City stock.

Chief Executive Officer Keith Creel said the railroad was running well, with service remaining strong across grain, intermodal and merchandise markets. He added that disciplined execution and a robust commercial pipeline left CPKC on track to meet its commitments for the year.

For investors, the quarter presents a mixed operating picture. Revenue momentum and higher adjusted earnings point to resilient demand, while the wider operating ratio shows that fuel inflation can absorb part of the benefit.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City stock: Revenue rises 15 percent amid fuel pressure
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported stronger revenue and adjusted earnings for the third quarter on October 28, while higher fuel costs put pressure on operating efficiency. The company said it remains on track to meet its commitments for 2026.

According to the CPKC earnings release, revenue rose 15 percent year over year to CAD 4.219 billion in the three months ended September 30, from CAD 3.661 billion a year earlier. Revenue ton-miles increased 6 percent, with freight revenue reaching CAD 4.139 billion.

Reported operating income increased to CAD 1.487 billion from CAD 1.336 billion. Reported diluted earnings per share rose 3 percent to CAD 1.04 from CAD 1.01. Core adjusted diluted EPS, a non-GAAP measure, increased 16 percent to CAD 1.28 from CAD 1.10.

The improvement in adjusted earnings came despite a sharper cost burden. CPKC's reported operating ratio rose to 64.8 percent from 63.5 percent, while the core adjusted ratio increased to 61.9 percent from 60.7 percent. The company said higher fuel prices affected the reported ratio by 170 basis points and the core adjusted ratio by 190 basis points.

Fuel expense climbed to CAD 667 million from CAD 415 million in the prior-year quarter. Net income attributable to controlling shareholders was CAD 917 million, compared with CAD 920 million a year earlier. The financial statements also show quarterly operating cash flow of CAD 1.550 billion, up from CAD 1.274 billion.

Chief Executive Officer Keith Creel said the railroad continued to grow in grain, intermodal and merchandise markets. He pointed to disciplined execution and a robust commercial pipeline as reasons for maintaining confidence in the company's full-year commitments.

Management expects mid-single-digit growth in revenue ton-miles for 2026 and continues to target low double-digit growth in core adjusted diluted EPS. Capital spending is expected to total approximately CAD 2.65 billion for the year. The company also expects a fourth-quarter operating ratio below 60 percent, supported by October volumes, network performance and a favorable weather outlook.

CPKC's reported operating ratio rose to 64.8 percent from 63.5 percent. The core adjusted ratio increased to 61.9 percent from 60.7 percent, with the company saying higher fuel prices affected the reported and adjusted figures.

CPKC net income falls despite rising revenues
sum: CALGARY, ALBERTA, CANADA —– Canadian Pacific Kansas City Railway (CPKC) on July 29 posted a decline in net income in the second quarter of 2026 despite a sharp increase in revenues.

Net income decreased 17% to C$1.02 billion in the April-June quarter compared with the same period in 2025. Meanwhile, revenues soared by 13% year on year to C$4.16 billion due to a bumper Canadian grain crop. The company’s grain transportation revenue rose by nearly 25% compared with the same period last year.

Grain freight revenue per revenue ton-mile rose from C$4.96 in the second quarter of 2025 to C$5.19 in the same quarter this year. The company transported 168,000 carloads of grain in the second quarter compared with 142,000 in the same period in 2025.

CPKC earlier this month announced that it had set a new June monthly record for transporting Canadian grain and grain products, moving 2.8 million tonnes. It beat the previous tonnage record set in June 2020. CPKC also set a second-quarter record for tonnage and carloads.

CPKC said operating ratio increased by 90 basis points to 64.6% from 63.7% in the second quarter of 2025, while core adjusted operating ratio increased 90 basis points to 61.6% from 60.7% in the previous year’s second quarter
Reported diluted EPS decreased 14% to $1.15, while core adjusted diluted EPS increased 13% to $1.27 year on year, beating the consensus estimate of $1.24.

Keith Creel, president and chief executive officer of CPKC, told analysts during a conference call that the company has benefited from being the only North American railway to span all three countries — Canada, the United States and Mexico.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited declares dividend
sum: CALGARY, AB, July 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Board of Directors of Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited (TSX: CP) (NYSE: CP) (CPKC) today declared a quarterly dividend of $0.268 per share on the outstanding Common Shares.

The dividend is payable on October 26, 2026, to holders of record at the close of business on September 25, 2026, and is an "eligible" dividend for purposes of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and any similar provincial/territorial legislation.

With its global headquarters in Calgary, Alta., Canada, CPKC is the first and only single-line transnational railway linking Canada, the United States and México, with unrivaled access to major ports from Vancouver to Atlantic Canada to the Gulf Coast to Lázaro Cárdenas, México. Stretching approximately 20,000 route miles and employing approximately 20,000 railroaders, CPKC provides North American customers unparalleled rail service and network reach to key markets across the continent. CPKC is growing with its customers, offering a suite of freight transportation services, logistics solutions and supply chain expertise. Visit cpkcr.com to learn more about the rail advantages of CPKC. CP-IR
